title: Tarte aux Poireaux
subtitle: A French leek and cream tart in a shortcrust case
excerpt: Leeks cooked down to soft ribbons with butter and a splash of white wine, bound in a cream custard and baked in a crisp shortcrust shell. Clean, gentle flavour with a tender set.
sourceNotes: Northern French baking tradition, adapted for a standard 23cm tart tin.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Cook the leeks up to a day ahead and refrigerate. Assemble and bake on the day.

content.text: Tarte aux poireaux is a mild, clean tart from northern France. The leeks cook slowly with butter until they collapse into soft green ribbons. Drain off any liquid that collects before adding the custard, or the base will go soft.

items.prepNote: trimmed, white and pale green parts, sliced into rounds

content.text: Roll the pastry to 3mm thick and line a 23cm loose-bottomed tart tin. Chill for 30 minutes.

Melt the butter in a wide frying pan over a low heat. Add the leeks with a pinch of salt. Cook for 10 minutes, stirring often, until softened. Pour in the wine and cook for 5 more minutes until absorbed. Tip into a sieve and press lightly to drain. Leave to cool.
Heat the oven to 190C. Line the pastry case with baking paper and baking beans. Blind bake for 15 minutes. Remove the paper and beans and bake for 5 more minutes until the base is dry.
Whisk the cream, eggs, and egg yolk together. Season with nutmeg and salt.
Spread the cooled leeks in the tart case. Scatter the gruyere over if using.
Pour the cream mixture over the leeks. Bake for 25 to 30 minutes until just set with a gentle wobble at the centre.
Rest in the tin for 10 minutes before unmoulding. Serve warm or at room temperature.

items.symptom: The base is wet under the leeks.
items.cause: The leeks still had too much moisture when they went in.
items.fix: Press the cooked leeks in a sieve for a few minutes and pat dry before spreading into the case.

items.symptom: The tart sinks in the middle when cut.
items.fix: Bake until the edges are fully set and only the very centre moves when you gently shake the tin.

items.symptom: The pastry shrinks away from the edges.
items.cause: The pastry was not chilled long enough before blind baking.
items.fix: Chill the lined tin for at least 30 minutes and make sure the pastry is pressed firmly into the corners.
